page_sections.intro: Credit card processing fees typically cost small businesses 2–3% of every sale. For a business doing $20,000/month in credit card sales, that's $400–$600 per month going to your processor. Surcharging — legally passing that fee to the customer — is now permitted in most US states and is one of the most effective ways to eliminate processing costs. This page explains how surcharging works, what GoDaddy Rate Saver is, and whether it's right for your business.

what_is_surcharging.title: What Is Surcharging?
what_is_surcharging.body: Surcharging is the practice of adding a small fee to a customer's transaction when they pay with a credit card — offsetting the processing cost the merchant would otherwise absorb. Surcharging is legal in most US states (with exceptions including Connecticut and Massachusetts) and is permitted under Visa and Mastercard network rules, subject to specific disclosure and cap requirements. Surcharging applies only to credit cards — you cannot surcharge debit card transactions under card network rules.

how_rate_saver_works.title: How GoDaddy Rate Saver Works
steps: Merchant enrolls in Rate Saver through their GoDaddy Payments account (eligibility verified at enrollment).
When a customer pays with a credit card in-person, the surcharge is automatically calculated and added to the transaction.
The customer pays the surcharge; the merchant's effective credit card processing rate is 0%.
Debit card transactions are not surcharged and process at 1.9% + $0.
Required disclosures are handled by GoDaddy's system at the point of sale.

eligibility_table.title: Rate Saver Eligibility at a Glance

faq.q: What is surcharging and is it legal for my business?
faq.a: Surcharging means adding a fee to a customer's bill when they pay with a credit card to offset your processing cost. It is legal in most US states. As of 2026, surcharging is prohibited in Connecticut and Massachusetts, and restricted in some other jurisdictions. Puerto Rico also prohibits surcharging. Card network rules (Visa, Mastercard) permit surcharging up to the merchant's actual cost of acceptance, subject to disclosure requirements. GoDaddy Rate Saver is designed to comply with applicable rules, but you should verify the rules for your specific state.

faq.q: How does GoDaddy Rate Saver work exactly?
faq.a: Rate Saver is GoDaddy's built-in surcharging program. When enabled, it automatically adds the credit card processing fee to the customer's transaction total at the point of sale. The merchant absorbs 0% of the credit card fee — the customer pays it. Debit card transactions are not surcharged and process at 1.9% + $0. Required customer disclosures are handled by GoDaddy's POS system.

faq.q: Can I use Rate Saver for my online store?
faq.a: No. Rate Saver applies to in-person transactions only. Online and ecommerce transactions are not eligible for Rate Saver and are processed at standard rates. If you have both an in-person and online business, Rate Saver will apply only to your in-person credit card sales.

faq.q: What rate do I pay on debit cards with Rate Saver?
faq.a: Debit card transactions cannot be surcharged under card network rules. With Rate Saver, debit card transactions process at 1.9% + $0 — which is still lower than most standard debit processing rates. The 0% rate applies to credit card transactions only.

faq.q: Do I have to tell customers about the surcharge?
faq.a: Yes. Card network rules and many state laws require merchants to disclose surcharging to customers before the transaction is completed. GoDaddy Rate Saver handles the required point-of-sale disclosure automatically through the Smart Terminal. You are also required to post notice at your store entrance. GoDaddy provides guidance on disclosure requirements at enrollment.

faq.q: Will surcharging hurt my customer relationships?
faq.a: This depends on your business type and customer base. Many businesses — including gas stations, medical offices, and service businesses — surcharge without significant customer pushback, especially when the fee is disclosed clearly upfront. Businesses with highly price-sensitive customers or in competitive retail environments may see more friction. Consider your specific customer base and competitive context before enabling Rate Saver.

faq.q: Am I eligible for Rate Saver if I'm in Connecticut or Massachusetts?
faq.a: No. Rate Saver is not available to merchants in Connecticut, Massachusetts, or Puerto Rico, where credit card surcharging is prohibited. If you are in one of these locations, you cannot use Rate Saver. GoDaddy's standard processing rates apply.

faq.q: How much money can I save with Rate Saver?
faq.a: If your business processes $15,000/month in credit card sales at a standard rate of 2.3%, you're currently paying approximately $345/month in processing fees on those transactions. With Rate Saver, your effective credit card processing cost drops to $0 on those sales. Debit card transactions would process at 1.9% + $0. Actual savings depend on your transaction mix (credit vs debit), volume, and average ticket size.

faq.q: Is there a fee to use Rate Saver?
faq.a: Rate Saver is included with eligible GoDaddy Payments plans — there is no separate monthly surcharging platform fee. This is different from some third-party surcharging solutions that charge a monthly fee on top of your processing costs. Verify current plan eligibility and pricing at godaddy.com/payments.

sections.heading: The Hidden Cost of Accepting Credit Cards
sections.body: The average small business pays 2–3% of every credit card sale in processing fees. For a coffee shop doing $25,000/month in sales, that's $500–$750 per month — $6,000–$9,000 per year — going to payment processors. Most business owners accept this as a cost of doing business. But there's a legal way to eliminate most of it: surcharging.

sections.heading: What Is Surcharging and Is It Legal?
sections.body: Surcharging means adding a small fee to a customer's transaction when they pay by credit card — passing the processing cost to the customer rather than absorbing it yourself. As of 2026, surcharging is legal in most US states. It is prohibited in Connecticut and Massachusetts, and not permitted in Puerto Rico. Card networks (Visa, Mastercard) allow surcharging up to the merchant's actual cost of acceptance, subject to disclosure requirements. You cannot surcharge debit card transactions under card network rules.

sections.heading: How Surcharging Works in Practice
sections.body: When a customer pays with a credit card at a surcharged business, they see a small additional fee — typically 2–3% — added to their total. The merchant must disclose the surcharge before the transaction (at the store entrance and at the point of sale). The customer can choose to pay with cash or debit to avoid the fee. In practice, most customers accept the surcharge, especially when it's disclosed clearly and the business provides good value.

sections.heading: How GoDaddy Rate Saver Works
sections.body: GoDaddy Rate Saver is a built-in surcharging program for eligible GoDaddy Payments merchants. When enabled, it automatically calculates and applies the surcharge to credit card transactions at the point of sale — no manual calculation or third-party surcharging software required. The merchant's effective credit card processing rate drops to 0%. Debit card transactions, which cannot be surcharged, process at 1.9% + $0. Rate Saver is not available in CT, MA, PR, or for ecommerce transactions.

sections.heading: Comparing Surcharging Programs: What to Look For
sections.body: Not all surcharging programs are equal. Some third-party surcharging solutions charge a monthly platform fee on top of your processing costs — which can eat into your savings. Key questions to ask: (1) Is surcharging built into my processor or do I need a third-party add-on? (2) Are there monthly fees for the surcharging feature? (3) Does the system handle required disclosures automatically? (4) What rate do I pay on debit cards? GoDaddy Rate Saver includes surcharging within eligible plans with no separate monthly surcharging fee.

sections.heading: Is Surcharging Right for Your Business?
sections.body: Surcharging works best for: service businesses (contractors, salons, medical offices), B2B businesses, and businesses where customers are accustomed to fee transparency. It may create friction for: high-volume retail with price-sensitive customers, businesses in competitive markets where competitors don't surcharge, or businesses where the customer experience is a primary differentiator. The decision is ultimately about your customer base and competitive context — not just the math.

sections.heading: The Bottom Line
sections.body: Surcharging is legal in most US states and is one of the most direct ways to reduce credit card processing costs. For eligible merchants, GoDaddy Rate Saver provides a built-in, no-extra-fee surcharging option that brings your effective credit card processing rate to 0%. If you're paying $300–$700/month in processing fees and your business is not in CT, MA, or PR, it's worth evaluating whether surcharging makes sense for your customers and your business model.

faq.q: Is it legal to charge customers a credit card fee?
faq.a: Yes, in most US states. Surcharging credit card transactions is legal under Visa and Mastercard network rules and permitted by state law in most states. As of 2026, it is prohibited in Connecticut and Massachusetts, and not permitted in Puerto Rico. You cannot surcharge debit card transactions under card network rules. Always verify current rules for your specific state before implementing surcharging.

faq.q: What's the difference between a surcharge and a convenience fee?
faq.a: A surcharge is a fee added specifically when a customer pays by credit card, offsetting the merchant's processing cost. A convenience fee is charged for the convenience of using a particular payment channel (such as paying online or by phone when in-person is the standard method). They are governed by different card network rules. Surcharging applies to all credit card transactions at a location; convenience fees apply to specific non-standard payment channels.

faq.q: How much can I charge as a surcharge?
faq.a: Card network rules cap surcharges at the merchant's actual cost of acceptance, with a maximum of 3% for Visa transactions (as of recent rule updates — verify current caps). The surcharge cannot exceed your actual processing cost. GoDaddy Rate Saver automatically calculates the correct surcharge amount to comply with network rules.

faq.q: Do I have to tell customers I'm surcharging?
faq.a: Yes. Card network rules require merchants to disclose surcharging at the store entrance and at the point of sale before the transaction is completed. Customers must have the opportunity to choose a different payment method (cash or debit) to avoid the surcharge. GoDaddy Rate Saver handles point-of-sale disclosure automatically. You are responsible for posting required signage at your entrance.

faq.q: Can I surcharge debit cards too?
faq.a: No. Card network rules prohibit surcharging debit card transactions, including prepaid debit cards. Surcharging applies to credit cards only. With GoDaddy Rate Saver, debit transactions process at 1.9% + $0 — which is still a competitive rate, but not 0%.

faq.q: Will customers stop coming to my business if I surcharge?
faq.a: Research and merchant experience suggest that most customers accept surcharges when they are disclosed clearly and the business provides good value. Gas stations have surcharged (cash vs credit pricing) for decades with minimal customer loss. The impact varies by business type — service businesses and B2B merchants typically see less friction than high-volume retail. Consider testing surcharging and monitoring customer feedback before making it permanent.

faq.q: What happens if I surcharge in a state where it's not allowed?
faq.a: Surcharging in a prohibited state (such as Connecticut or Massachusetts) violates state law and card network rules, and can result in fines, card network penalties, and potential legal liability. GoDaddy Rate Saver automatically blocks enrollment for merchants in ineligible states. If you are unsure whether surcharging is permitted in your state, consult legal counsel before implementing any surcharging program.

faq.q: Are there other ways to reduce processing fees besides surcharging?
faq.a: Yes. Other strategies include: (1) negotiating interchange-plus pricing if you have high volume, (2) encouraging cash or debit payments with a cash discount program (different from surcharging — verify rules), (3) choosing a processor with lower base rates like GoDaddy's 2.3% + $0 in-person rate, and (4) reducing keyed-in transactions which carry higher rates. Surcharging is the most direct way to eliminate credit card fees entirely for eligible merchants.

faq.q: Can I use GoDaddy Payments for a food truck or market stall?

faq.q: Does GoDaddy POS work for a cafe with a simple menu?
faq.a: Yes. GoDaddy POS handles item catalogs, modifiers, and counter-service workflows suitable for most cafes and quick-service food businesses. It is not designed for full-service restaurant table management or complex kitchen display workflows. If your cafe is counter-service with a straightforward menu, GoDaddy POS is a capable and cost-effective option.

faq.q: Can I pass credit card fees to my coffee shop customers?

Debit transactions process at 1.9% + $0. Rate Saver is not available in CT, MA, PR, or for ecommerce. faq.q: Is Toast better than GoDaddy for a small restaurant?

faq.q: How does GoDaddy POS compare to Square for a high-volume cafe?

Square's $0.15 flat fee is proportionally expensive on $4–$6 transactions. At 200 transactions/day averaging $5, GoDaddy saves approximately $1,000/month compared to Square's rate. Square's free starter hardware and strong offline mode are advantages for new or mobile operations.

faq.q: What hardware do I need to use GoDaddy Payments in my cafe?
faq.a: GoDaddy Payments uses the GoDaddy Smart Terminal, a countertop device with a customer-facing display and built-in receipt printer. It accepts chip, swipe, and contactless (tap-to-pay) payments. Hardware purchase is required — there is no free starter device. For a counter-service cafe, the Smart Terminal is designed to handle fast transaction throughput at the register.

faq.q: Does GoDaddy POS have inventory management for a food business?
faq.a: GoDaddy POS includes basic item catalog and inventory tracking. For complex food inventory management — including ingredient-level tracking, recipe costing, or waste management — you may need a dedicated inventory management tool integrated with your POS. Verify GoDaddy's current inventory features at godaddy.com/payments before making a decision based on inventory needs.
